patients.summary: Retired carpenter with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary disease and chronic back pain on long-term morphine who joins in 2020, develops paroxysmal AF on warfarin and stage IV right colon cancer in 2022, has an appendectomy in 2023 and ischemic strokes in 2024 and 2025, and is in hospital with a warfarin-associated intracerebral hemorrhage at today.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Arthur Crowley, 67, Florence. His doctor of many years is retiring at the end of September and a neighbor recommended us. Medicare plus a supplement. Explained the membership model and fee; he wants to go ahead. Takes a long-acting pain medicine for his back and asked whether we would keep prescribing it. Told him the physician reviews that at the first visit. New patient visit set for 9/14 at 9:00. Records release faxed to his current office. Asked him to bring all his medicine bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Arthur is a 67 year old retired carpenter here to establish care; his longtime PCP is retiring. Wife with him for the second half of the visit.

He says he has had blood pressure trouble and sugar diabetes for a good many years, neither giving him symptoms. Some years back he had chest discomfort and was sent for a heart catheterization at an outside hospital; he was told he had coronary disease, no stent, and to stay on aspirin and the statin. No chest pain since. Back: decades of framing and roofing, low back pain that has been daily for years, no leg weakness, no bladder or bowel trouble. Has been on long-acting morphine 30 mg twice a day under his prior doctor for a long time; says it lets him do yard work and short walks. Does not take extra doses, no early refills by his account.

PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease (diagnostic cath, medical management), chronic low back pain.
PSH: diagnostic cardiac catheterization. No other operations.
Meds (bottles reviewed): metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily, morphine ER 30 mg q12h.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father had an MI at 72. Mother had an ischemic stroke at 78. A paternal uncle had colon cancer found at 75.
SH: married, lives with wife in Florence. Carpenter for about 40 years, retired. Smoked roughly a pack a day for 30 years, stopped in 2012. A drink or two a month.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. Heart rate regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Lumbar paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative both sides, strength and reflexes symmetric. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt throughout, pulses palpable. No edema.

Assessment and plan:
1. Hypertension: around goal today on lisinopril and HCTZ. Continue. BMP.
2. Type 2 diabetes on metformin: A1c, urine albumin today. Eye exam is due; he will book with his optometrist.
3. CAD, stable without angina: aspirin and atorvastatin 40 continue. Lipids.
4. Chronic low back pain on long-term morphine: reviewed state prescription monitoring report, single prescriber and pharmacy, fills on time. Controlled-substance agreement reviewed and signed. Will continue ER morphine 30 mg q12h, monthly scripts from this office. Pain 4/10 today.
5. Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2012: eligible for annual low-dose CT; he would rather wait until his records arrive and then schedule. Will revisit in December.
6. Health maintenance: hepatitis C and HIV screening today. Prior office's records requested for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Flu shot when it arrives.

Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Arthur, your labs from Monday look good. Kidney function and potassium are normal, the A1c is right about where we want it, and the bad cholesterol is in good range on your atorvastatin. Urine protein is normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. No changes to your medicines.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
38 pages received by fax from the patient's previous primary care office, scanned. Summary for chart, prepared by the physician:
- Hypertension and type 2 diabetes followed there for years on the current regimen.
- Diagnostic cardiac catheterization at an outside hospital, managed medically afterward; the cath report itself is not in the packet.
- Chronic low back pain on ER morphine 30 mg twice daily, with a signed pain agreement on file there.
- Colonoscopy 2012: no polyps.
- Tdap 2016. No shingles or pneumococcal vaccines documented.
- Allergies: none.
Nothing in the packet changes the current plan.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine 0.7 mL IM, left deltoid. Screening questions negative. VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, left after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Morphine refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient called for his monthly morphine ER. Last fill 10/6. Prescription monitoring checked, no other prescribers. Routed to PCP, e-prescribed for 30 days. He was told it would be at his usual pharmacy by noon.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of HTN, diabetes, back pain.

Feeling fine. Splitting wood most weekends, back about the same, 4/10 most days. Taking everything as listed, no missed doses he can think of. No chest pain, no breathlessness on hills. Home sugars when he checks run 120s to 150s fasting.

Records from his old office reviewed; colonoscopy 2012 without polyps, so next one is due around 2022.

Exam: BP as charted. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- HTN: at goal, continue.
- DM2: A1c at goal in September, continue metformin.
- Chronic LBP / long-term opioid: stable function, no aberrant behavior, PDMP reviewed. Continue ER morphine.
- Lung screening: discussed benefits, false positives and radiation; he would like to do it. Low-dose CT ordered.
- Shingles vaccine next visit.

RTC 3 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Lung parenchyma is unremarkable. Airways patent. Heart normal in size. Coronary artery calcification present, consistent with known coronary disease. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: LDCT negative, Lung-RADS 1. Coronary calcium noted, already known CAD on statin. Patient notified through the portal; repeat next December.

documents.title: COVID vaccine dose 1, outside
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient sent a photo of his vaccine card: Moderna dose 1 given today at a retail pharmacy clinic. Entered into the immunization record. Dose 2 scheduled there for late February.

documents.title: COVID vaccine dose 2, outside
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Dose 2 Moderna recorded from the state registry. Patient said by portal he felt tired and achy the next day only.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Both COVID shots done. Back pain unchanged, managing. No chest symptoms.
BP a touch above where I'd like on recheck; he admits to a lot of ham at the holidays. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.
Plan: continue current meds, cut back salt, BMP and A1c today. Shingrix #1 given, second in 2 to 6 months. Morphine continued, PDMP reviewed.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated diabetic eye examination, 04/13/2021.
Visual acuity 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Pressures normal. Lens: mild nuclear changes both eyes. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, macula flat, no hemorrhages or exudates.
Impression: type 2 diabetes without retinopathy. Recheck in one year.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Quick check-in. Spring labs fine, A1c holding. Building a porch railing for a friend, back sore after but no new symptoms. No chest pain. Taking meds.
Exam unremarkable, BP as charted.
Shingrix #2 today, series complete. Morphine ER continued. Physical in September.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need the metformin and the atorvastatin renewed, the pharmacy says no refills left. Thanks. Art

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Both sent to your pharmacy with a year of refills. Have a good week.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare wellness visit.

Function: independent in everything, still drives, does his own carpentry projects. Hearing fine in a quiet room. No falls this year. Sleeps 6 to 7 hours. Lives with wife, two-story house, stairs without trouble.
Mood: PHQ-2 0. Alcohol: AUDIT-C 1.
Cognition: three-word recall and clock draw normal.
Advance directive: wife is health care proxy; he will bring a copy.

Problems and meds reviewed, unchanged. Back pain stable on ER morphine, agreement current, PDMP reviewed.
Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Feet: intact sensation, good pulses, no lesions.

Screening/prevention:
- Colon: last colonoscopy 2012 normal; due next year, will refer early 2022.
- Lung: repeat LDCT in December.
- Vaccines: flu at nurse visit in October; Shingrix complete; COVID booster at the pharmacy when eligible; pneumococcal next year.
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin.
Personalized plan given in writing.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu 0.7 mL IM, right deltoid. He had his Moderna booster at the pharmacy on 10/1; card seen, added to the record. No reactions to either.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 11:00. Called; wife answered and said he was out at a job site helping a friend and lost track of the day. Rebooked for 12/14.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sorry about last week, he says. Feels well, regular heartbeat by his account, no chest pain. Back 4/10.
September labs: A1c up slightly, LDL in range, kidney function normal, urine albumin normal.
Exam: regular rhythm, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN and DM2 stable on current meds, A1c a bit higher, he knows the holidays are coming. Long-term opioid unchanged, PDMP reviewed, refill sent. Annual LDCT reordered. Colonoscopy referral next visit. RTC 3 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose CT chest without contrast. Comparison 12/17/2020. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Central airways clear. Heart size normal; coronary artery calcification is unchanged. No adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Second LDCT negative. Message sent to patient.

reports.text: Atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate about 90. Normal axis. QRS narrow. No acute ST or T wave changes. No prior tracing for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Palpitations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in on a same-day slot. For about six weeks he has had spells of his heart fluttering, sometimes an hour, sometimes most of an afternoon, and he has felt more worn out than usual. No chest pain, no fainting, not short of breath. No caffeine change. Wife noticed his pulse jumping when she held his wrist.

Exam: pulse irregularly irregular. BP as charted. No murmur. Lungs clear. No leg swelling. Weight down a couple of pounds since fall.

ECG in office: atrial fibrillation, rate controlled, no ischemic changes.

A/P: new atrial fibrillation in a 69 year old with hypertension, diabetes and CAD. Stroke risk is clearly elevated and he will need anticoagulation; I would like cardiology to see him promptly and decide on the anticoagulant and any rate or rhythm strategy. Urgent referral placed, they can see him February 1. Return or go to the ED for chest pain, fainting or a racing heart that doesn't settle. Continue current meds including aspirin for now.

medications.sig: Take as directed per INR; currently 5 mg by mouth daily

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient cardiology consultation. Date of visit: 02/01/2022.
Reason for referral: atrial fibrillation found by his primary care physician.

Mr. Crowley, 69, describes roughly two months of on-and-off palpitations together with fatigue. He has had no chest pain, no shortness of breath and no fainting.

History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease after a diagnostic catheterization in the past, chronic low back pain. Surgical: diagnostic cardiac catheterization.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, aspirin 81 mg daily, morphine sulfate ER 30 mg twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father MI at 72, mother ischemic stroke at 78, paternal uncle colon cancer at 75.
Social: retired carpenter, former smoker with 30 pack-years who stopped 10 years ago, alcohol 1 to 2 drinks a month.

Exam: BP 142/88. Heart rate 88, irregularly irregular. No added heart sounds, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Labs: hemoglobin A1c 7.2%, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, INR 1.0.
ECG: atrial fibrillation.

Assessment: atrial fibrillation, rate acceptable at rest. CHA2DS2-VASc score 4 (hypertension, diabetes, vascular disease, age 65 to 74), well above the threshold for anticoagulation.
Plan:
1. Begin warfarin 5 mg daily, dose to be adjusted to an INR of 2 to 3. His primary care office will follow INRs; first check in one week.
2. Transthoracic echocardiogram.
3. Continue his other medications.
4. Follow up here as needed; sooner for symptoms.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: First INR since warfarin 5 mg daily started 2/1. INR 1.5, expected this early. No bleeding or bruising. Reviewed warfarin teaching with patient and wife: consistent greens, no new supplements, alcohol kept light, tell us about any antibiotic. Continue 5 mg daily. Recheck 2 weeks. PCP aware.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No bleeding. Palpitations less frequent he thinks. Continue 5 mg daily, 35 mg/week. Recheck 3 weeks.

reports.text: Complete transthoracic study. Rhythm atrial fibrillation during the study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function, LVEF 55-60%, no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Left atrium normal in size. Right atrium normal. Aortic, mitral and tricuspid valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. Aortic root normal. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and function, LVEF 55-60%. No significant valve disease. Normal atrial size.

documents.title: Echo report received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Outside echo from cardiology: normal heart function, valves fine, atria normal. Portal note to patient.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No bleeding. Mentions his stomach has been off on and off and he has dropped some weight; advised he raise it with PCP, offered appointment, booked 4/5. Warfarin unchanged. Recheck with that visit or in 4 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: weight loss, iron deficiency anemia, dark stools

documents.title: Weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since around New Year's he has had an achy, come-and-go discomfort in the belly, nothing sharp, and his stools have been looser than usual with a feeling he hasn't finished. A few times the stool looked dark, almost black. No bright red blood. Appetite somewhat down. He has lost about 15 pounds without trying since the fall. No fever, no vomiting. Started warfarin in February.

Exam: looks thinner. Conjunctivae a little pale. Abdomen soft, mild fullness and tenderness on the right side without guarding, no mass I can feel, no liver edge. Rectal deferred to GI. Heart irregular, rate fine. Lungs clear.

Labs back this afternoon: hemoglobin 10.4, microcytic; ferritin 7. INR in range.

A/P
1. Iron deficiency anemia with weight loss, change in bowel habit and dark stools, on anticoagulation: needs prompt GI evaluation for a GI source; colonoscopy is due regardless. Urgent GI referral placed and I called their office; seen 4/28. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. Warfarin continued for now given his stroke risk; he and his wife know to go to the ED for black tarry stools, vomiting blood or lightheadedness.
2. AF on warfarin: INR in range.
Rest unchanged. Follow up after GI.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No further dark stools this week. GI visit 4/28; GI office will give instructions on holding warfarin around a colonoscopy. Continue current dose.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Liver: multiple hypodense lesions in the right hepatic lobe. Left lobe without focal lesion. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically, no hydronephrosis. Ascending colon wall thickening with an irregular mass at the site of the endoscopic finding. Appendix is normal. No ascites. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. No free air.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon mass with multiple right hepatic lobe hypodense lesions, concerning for metastatic disease.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Several small pulmonary nodules in both lungs, new compared with the low-dose screening CT of 12/21/2021. No effusion. No mediastinal mass. Heart normal in size. Coronary calcification.
reports.conclusion: Several small bilateral pulmonary nodules, new since 12/2021, concerning for metastases.

reports.text: Specimen: ascending colon mass, endoscopic biopsies. Microscopic: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, in fragments of colonic mucosa.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon, biopsy: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and procedure
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology. Date of service: 04/28/2022.

Referred for unintentional weight loss and on-and-off abdominal discomfort over three months, about three months after his February cardiology visit for new atrial fibrillation. He also reports looser stools at times, a sense of incomplete evacuation, and dark stools on a few occasions without frank rectal bleeding. Diabetes and hypertension are well controlled.

Social: carpenter for 40 years, quit smoking a decade ago after 30 pack-years.
Meds: per referral, including warfarin (held for the procedure per our protocol), aspirin, metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, ER morphine, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

Labs: iron deficiency anemia confirmed.
Colonoscopy: ulcerated, obstructing mass in the ascending colon; the scope could not be passed beyond it. Biopsies taken.
Pathology: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma.
CT abdomen/pelvis and chest: multiple hypodense lesions in the right lobe of the liver and several small nodules in both lungs, consistent with metastatic disease.

Impression: right-sided colon adenocarcinoma with liver and lung lesions.
Plan: urgent oncology referral; appointment arranged. Resume warfarin tonight. Results reviewed with patient and his wife.

documents.title: Call with patient and wife
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called after reading the GI letter. He and his wife already heard the diagnosis from GI. Quiet but composed; she had most of the questions. Talked through what a spread to the liver and lungs means, that oncology will lay out treatment, and that we stay involved for everything else. Oncology appointment confirmed for 5/17. He asked whether he'd done something wrong by waiting on the colonoscopy; reassured. Offered a visit any time. Will keep the INR checks going here.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology new patient consultation. Visit date 05/17/2022.

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending (right) colon, moderately differentiated, with multiple right hepatic lobe lesions and bilateral pulmonary nodules on staging CT: clinical stage IV.

He is a 69 year old retired carpenter, fully active, ECOG 0 to 1, with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary disease, atrial fibrillation on warfarin and chronic back pain on ER morphine. NKDA.
CEA 48.2 ng/mL.

Discussion: the disease is not resectable for cure at this time. The goals of systemic therapy (control, symptom relief, time) were reviewed with him and his wife. Given his cardiac history and anticoagulation, we will start with FOLFOX alone.
Plan:
- Port placement by interventional radiology, scheduled 5/20.
- FOLFOX every 14 days, 12 cycles planned, starting 5/24.
- Ondansetron for nausea as needed.
- Fluorouracil can raise the INR; please check INR more often during treatment and let us know of large swings.
- Restaging CT after cycle 12.
We will keep you informed.

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Fill history review
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Ran outside fill history while preparing the morphine refill. New fill 5/23 from the oncology office: ondansetron 4 mg ODT, #30. Added to his medication list as prescribed elsewhere. Morphine ER last filled 5/3, refill routed to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three cycles of FOLFOX in so far through his new port. Tired for two or three days after each, some queasiness that the dissolving tablets handle. Eating smaller meals. Belly discomfort a little less. Wife drives him to infusions.

Oncology's CBC last week showed the hemoglobin coming up on iron. Fasting sugars lower, 100s to 120s; A1c today. INR in range today.

Exam: port site right upper chest clean, healed. Weight down a little more. Heart irregular, rate controlled. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

A/P
- Metastatic right colon cancer on FOLFOX, managed by oncology.
- AF on warfarin: INR in range on 5-FU, which can push it up; will check every 2 to 3 weeks during chemo.
- DM2: eating less, sugars lower; keep metformin for now, call for any reading under 70.
- Iron deficiency anemia: improving, continue iron.
- Back pain stable on ER morphine; PDMP reviewed.
See in 2 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR above range. No bleeding, no new bruises, gums fine. Mid-chemo. Per PCP: take 2.5 mg (half tablet) on Mondays and Fridays, 5 mg other days (30 mg/week). Recheck 2 weeks. Instructions read back by wife.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit: 07/22/2022.

Chief complaint: racing heart and lightheaded.
HPI: man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin and colon cancer on chemotherapy, here with palpitations and lightheadedness that came on suddenly three hours before arrival.
PMH: long-standing hypertension, coronary artery disease, diabetes, AF, colon cancer. Meds include lisinopril and aspirin, warfarin; full list per patient. NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago. Rare alcohol. Retired carpenter.

Exam: pulse 120, irregularly irregular. BP 130/84. No jugular venous distention. No peripheral edema. Lungs clear.
ECG: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, rate about 120, no acute ST changes.

Course: diltiazem IV in the department; ventricular rate settled to the 80s and the lightheadedness resolved. Observed, stable.
Disposition: discharged home. Continue home medications. Follow up with PCP this week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED on 7/22 for fast AF; IV diltiazem there, rate came down and he went home the same day. ED note reviewed. No episodes since, no lightheadedness. Seven cycles of FOLFOX done.

Exam: heart irregular, rate controlled. BP as charted. Lungs clear. No edema.
INR in range on the adjusted dose.

A/P: AF, one episode of rapid rate during chemotherapy, controlled at rest now; continue warfarin, call or go to the ED for sustained racing or lightheadedness. INR every 2 to 3 weeks. Rest unchanged.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range on 30 mg/week. No bleeding. Continue. Recheck 3 weeks or with next visit.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual dilated exam 09/14/2022. Acuity 20/25 both eyes with correction. No diabetic retinopathy either eye. Mild cataract changes, not visually significant. Return in 12 months. Medications reviewed including warfarin. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Ten of twelve cycles done. Fatigue the main thing. No more racing heart since July. Bowels more regular, no dark stools. Oncology says his blood count is nearly normal.

Exam: weight steady. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear. Port site fine. Feet: sensation intact, pulses present.
PHQ-2 1; low days around infusions but not depressed, he says.

A/P
- Colon cancer: finishing FOLFOX in November, restaging after.
- AF/warfarin: INR in range. Continue 30 mg/week.
- DM2: A1c lower in June with the weight loss. Continue metformin.
- HTN: fine.
- CAD: lipids today.
- Vaccines: high-dose flu and PCV20 today. Bivalent COVID at pharmacy.
- Iron: continue until hemoglobin normal.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: COVID bivalent booster, outside
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Bivalent Moderna booster 10/14 at a retail pharmacy, pulled from the state registry and added.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR slightly low. Last chemo cycle was last week. No missed doses. Per PCP, back to 5 mg daily (35 mg/week) now that infusions are ending. Recheck 2 to 3 weeks.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Restaging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Comparison 04/28/2022. Right hepatic lobe hypodense lesions are fewer and smaller. Bilateral small pulmonary nodules are smaller, several no longer seen. Ascending colon wall thickening decreased. Appendix normal. No new lesion. No ascites or adenopathy. Port catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction.
reports.conclusion: Partial response of hepatic and pulmonary metastases and the ascending colon primary. No new disease.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology follow-up, 12/13/2022.
Completed 12 cycles of FOLFOX on 11/1. Fatigue improving. Restaging CT 12/8 shows partial response in the liver, lungs and primary. CEA 7.9, down from 48.2.
Plan, agreed with patient and wife: treatment break with CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and CEA every 3 to 4 months; restart therapy at progression. Port to be flushed every 6 to 8 weeks here. Ondansetron no longer needed.
Thank you for co-managing his other conditions.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range on 35 mg/week. No bleeding. On a chemo break, feeling stronger. Recheck 4 to 6 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Tells me he was in the ED at the end of January, the 30th, with his heart racing again and some breathlessness. They gave him something in the IV, it slowed down, and he went home that night. No papers with him and nothing has come to us; release signed today and request faxed.
Since then fine. No chest pain. Energy back since chemo stopped. Eating well, weight creeping up. Stools normal, no dark stools. He says the ED told him his blood count was normal.

Exam: irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear. No edema. Port site clean.

A/P
- AF, second ED visit for rapid rate; resting rate fine today. Continue warfarin. Will review ED record when it arrives.
- Iron deficiency anemia: hemoglobin reportedly normal; stop ferrous sulfate. Recheck CBC with spring labs.
- DM2: A1c and BMP today.
- Colon cancer: on treatment break, CT every 3 to 4 months with oncology.
- Back pain: stable on ER morphine, PDMP reviewed, agreement renewed.
RTC 3 months, physical.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR a bit above range. No bleeding. Admits he's been skipping salads this winter. Hold tonight's dose, then resume 35 mg/week. Recheck 2 weeks.

documents.title: Anticoagulation follow-up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called for the 2-week recheck; he says he was at an oncology CT and blood draw last week and could not fit in another trip. Will come with his May physical. Reinforced that he should not skip checks; he agreed to call with any bleeding.

reports.text: No P waves. Irregularly irregular R-R intervals. Ventricular rate about 110. Narrow QRS. No acute ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received on request)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department visit 01/30/2023, sent in response to records request.

CC: palpitations, mild shortness of breath.
HPI: patient with recurrent atrial fibrillation, three hours of palpitations and mild dyspnea. Denies chest pain, dizziness or syncope.

Regional hospital. Admitted 07/21/2023, discharged 07/24/2023.

Presentation: right lower quadrant pain since that morning, sharp and constant and worse with movement, in a man with metastatic ascending colon cancer (on a treatment break) and atrial fibrillation on warfarin. Home medications included sustained-release morphine, lisinopril and metformin; full list reconciled. NKDA.
ED vitals: temperature 37.8 C, HR 102, RR 28, BP 138/86, SpO2 98% on room air.
Exam: rebound tenderness and guarding in the right lower quadrant; bowel sounds normal.
Labs: WBC 14,000/uL, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 250,000/uL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, BUN 18 mg/dL, glucose 160 mg/dL. Arterial gas (obtained for tachypnea): pH 7.52, PaCO2 28, HCO3 24, PaO2 95, consistent with respiratory alkalosis from pain.
CT: acute appendicitis without perforation; known colon primary and liver lesions unchanged.

Course: warfarin held and INR reversed with IV vitamin K. Open appendectomy through a right lower quadrant incision the evening of 7/21; acute appendicitis, no tumor on pathology. Recovery uneventful, diet advanced, pain controlled on his home morphine. Warfarin resumed 7/23.

Discharge diagnosis: acute appendicitis, status post open appendectomy.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 to 2 weeks with INR; surgical clinic in 2 weeks for wound check.

IV alteplase given.

Course: about 48 hours later he became increasingly drowsy and confused, with worse left-sided weakness. Vitals then BP 155/85, HR 88, temperature 37.1 C. Emergent CT head: evolving right hemisphere infarct with edema and mild local mass effect, no hemorrhage. Transferred to the neuro ICU, head of bed elevated, close neuro checks; alertness improved over the following days without further intervention. Returned to the stroke unit.
Warfarin restarted 08/04 with INR monitoring; aspirin and atorvastatin continued.

Diagnosis: recurrent acute ischemic stroke, right hemisphere, cardioembolic with subtherapeutic INR.
At discharge: alert, speech mildly slurred and improving, mild left-sided weakness, walking with therapy.
Discharge medications: warfarin (dose per INR), aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, morphine sulfate ER 30 mg twice daily. NKDA.

documents.title: Neurocritical care admission note
documents.author: neurocritical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital neurocritical care unit, admission history and physical, 08/03/2026. Faxed to PCP.

CC: left-sided weakness and slurred speech, then airway compromise.
HPI: 73 year old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin and two prior ischemic strokes, with left-sided weakness and slurred speech beginning about two hours before arrival. His wife reports he was in his usual health until that morning.
PMH: atrial fibrillation; ischemic strokes 2024 and 2025; metastatic right colon adenocarcinoma on observation; hypertension; type 2 diabetes; coronary artery disease; chronic low back pain. PSH: open appendectomy, diagnostic cardiac catheterization, port.
Home medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily, morphine sulfate ER 30 mg BID, warfarin. NKDA.
FH: father MI at 72; mother ischemic stroke at 78; paternal uncle colon cancer at 75.
SH: retired carpenter; former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago; alcohol 1 to 2 drinks a month.

Exam on arrival: BP 190/100, HR 78, irregularly irregular. Alert but anxious. Left facial droop, left hemiparesis, dysarthria.
Labs: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 250,000/uL, INR 3.2, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, BUN 14 mg/dL.
CT head: right basal ganglia hemorrhage without intraventricular extension.

ED and ICU course: alertness declined in the ED and he could no longer protect his airway; intubated. Warfarin reversed with 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate and IV vitamin K. Nicardipine infusion for blood pressure. Warfarin and aspirin held.
Assessment: warfarin-associated intracerebral hemorrhage, right basal ganglia, with airway compromise.
Plan: neurocritical care admission, repeat imaging, ventilator management, family meeting.
